text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing steady resident memory growth on prod-kv-gpu when sessions go long (>10k tokens). Started after last runtime rollout (kernel selector + new batching heuristics). not a spike, a slow climb over hours.

raj: I reproduced on staging this morning. heap viewers show many small live allocations in KV slabs that never get freed. looks like "sticky buffers" — slots get marked dead but remain attached to slab chains. :thinking:

olivia: do you have a profile or flamegraph?

maria: attaching short dump from 03:15 UTC (condensed):
```
kv_cache.total_slots: 2,048,000
kv_cache.live_slots: 1,837,412
kv_cache.free_slots: 210,588
kv_slab_small.count: 1,120,456
kv_slab_small.live_pct: 82.3
kv_slab_medium.count: 512,000
kv_slab_large.count: 256,000
alloc_window_ms: 180
small_block_size: 64
```
There are lots of `small` slabs at high live_pct; reclamation rate is ~3%/hr.

ciara: hmm. after the batching change we increased `alloc_window_ms` from 50->180 to allow longer coalescing for throughput. Could that delay reclamation?

raj: possibly. We also changed kernel selector to prefer packed kernels which keep KV handles pinned longer for prefetch. Pinning + longer alloc window = windows where old KV blocks can't be recycled.

tim: I sketched a timeline: requests with >8k tokens keep KV frames pinned across background async tasks. if compaction is opportunistic and only checks free ratio on allocation, it won't trigger for those long-lived pins.

perf-bot: nightly-profile (1778880000) uploaded: `kv_reclaim_attempts: 120` `kv_compactions: 2` `avg_reclaim_latency_ms: 420` `peak_rss_gb: 94.7`

olivia: can you grep for references to "pin" in the allocator? maybe some code path forgot to clear `owner_ref` on error.

maria: did quick grep: found `owner_ref` being set in `kv_attach_for_prefetch()` and only cleared on success path. if prefetch aborted early (timeout), we may never clear.

ciara: that smells like a bug. but even if fixed, we still need better heuristic: compaction should consider `virtual_live_pct` (live + pinned) and not just free slots.

raj: proposal: 1) short-term: back out alloc_window bump to 60ms on a subset of hosts (canary) 2) medium: add aggressive compaction pass that treats pinned-after-T ms as reclaimable candidate for small slabs 3) long-term: add periodic slab defrag that relocates live slots to free large slabs and returns empty small slabs to OS.

tim: for 2) we need to be careful — relocating live slots touches KV indices and could add latency. maybe do it off-critical-path and limit to <1% CPU of host.

maria: experiment config snippet I suggest for canary (apply to prod-kv-gpu-canary):
```
kv.alloc_window_ms = 60
kv.small_block_max = 48
kv.compaction.mode = incremental
kv.compaction.interval_s = 120
kv.pinned_threshold_ms = 3000
```
Lowering `small_block_max` will force medium slabs and may reduce fragmentation in practice.

olivia: also add metric `kv.pinned_slots_ratio` and `kv.slab_fragmentation_index` so we can alert earlier.

perf-bot: test-run queued: `kv-stress-longctx --duration 6h --max-tokens 20000 --concurrency 40` on canary pool. id=run-2026-03-18-01

ciara: I'll own the canary rollout and run the stress. timeline: start tonight 02:00 UTC, watch for 4h. rollback if rss > +15% vs baseline or compaction ops spike > 10x.

raj: small FYI — I also noticed we have `slab_cache` per-NUMA node that isn't shared; when one NUMA gets fragmented we still have free in other nodes. We might benefit from cross-node reclaim before growing resident.

maria: good call. add `kv.cross_numa_reclaim=true` to the canary?

ciara: yes will add.

tim: action items summary: ciara-run canary + stress; raj to instrument `owner_ref` clear-path & add unit test; olivia to add metrics/alerts; maria to draft rollback plan and comms to customer-facing SRE channel.

maria: thanks team. tagging @deploy-bot to hold the rollout note. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout note created: "kv-sticky-buffers remedy (canary)" scheduled 02:00 UTC.

maria: I'll post results in this thread once run-2026-03-18-01 completes.

olivia: thanks — if the pinned bug is real we should prioritize a patch rather than only heuristics.

raj: agreed. prioritizing bugfix after we capture repro.

ciara: ack.

maria: end of thread for now.
